area: Traffic realism (vehicle motion, demand, routing, intersections) in the pure-Python mock pipeline (src/scms_sim_ref/mock_pipeline/)
current_state:
TWO MOBILITY REGIMES (run.py):

1) FIXED-FLEET (default, traffic_flow=False): N vehicles (default 12) exist for the whole run on a "linear" pseudo-road. Vehicle.true_state() (run.py:650-668) is closed-form kinematics: spawn at x=vid*20, lane_y=(vid%4)*4 (run.py:1590), straight heading with random direction ±0.25 rad (run.py:1593), constant speed = nominal_speed*(0.85+0.3*U) * class-mult * weather-mult (run.py:1584-1588), plus a sinusoidal "lane wander" (amp ≤1.5 m, run.py:1594, 656-668). NO car-following, NO interaction, vehicles pass through each other. n_steps=40, dt=1.0 s default (run.py:274-276).

2) FLOW MODE (opt-in, traffic_flow=True): vehicles spawn/despawn on a road network and follow routed Trips with IDM car-following.

CAR-FOLLOWING: IDM in _idm_accel (run.py:2274-2283): a = a_max*(1-(v/v0)^4-(s*/s)^2), s* = s0 + max(0, v*T + v*dv/(2*sqrt(a*b))); accel clamped to [-6, a_max]. Defaults: idm_accel=1.5, idm_decel=2.0, T=1.3 s, s0=2.5 m, lookahead 70 m (run.py:429-434). Per-class overrides from VEHICLE_TYPES (run.py:142-147): car a=1.8/b=2.5/L=4.5, motorcycle 2.5/3.0/2.2, truck 0.8/1.5/12.0, bus 0.9/1.6/12.0. Leader search in car_follow (run.py:2442-2461): spatial hash (cell=lookahead), same-direction only (heading diff ≤45°, run.py:2458), lateral tolerance hard-coded ±3.0 m (run.py:2458) — cross traffic is INVISIBLE to IDM. Integration: Euler, order-independent via start-of-step snapshot (run.py:2406-2407), speed clamped to per-edge cap (run.py:2485-2490), arc-length s_pos advanced, position from trip.at_distance (run.py:2491-2495).

LANE MODEL: global n_lanes per config for ALL roads (run.py:420), lane = perpendicular offset (lane_idx-(n-1)/2)*lane_width from the centerline (run.py:1600-1603, 2499-2502). Discretionary MOBIL lane changes are OPT-IN and OFF by default (lane_changes=False, run.py:453-466): _mobil_decide (run.py:2285-2377) with politeness 0.2, threshold 0.2 m/s², safety veto at 4 m/s² follower decel, smoothstep lateral transition over ≥2.5 s producing a capped ~12° heading swing (run.py:2258, 2364-2370), reconsideration ~1/s per driver (run.py:2255, 2384-2389). NO mandatory lane changes (turns, merges, lane drops).

SPAWNING/DEMAND (run.py:1700-1751): Poisson arrivals (expovariate) at arrival_rate (default 2/s), thinned by demand_mult(frac) where frac = t/total_time: "rush" = two Gaussian peaks at 25%/75% OF THE RUN DURATION (run.py:1705-1711) — a synthetic day compressed into the run, no wall-clock; "night" = 0.15+0.25*frac; "uniform" = 1. Scenario events can multiply demand mid-run (run.py:1493-1498). Attacker/faulty/colluder assignment is an i.i.d. coin at spawn (run.py:1737-1739). Desired speed U(trip_speed_min=8, trip_speed_max=18) m/s (run.py:1740). Rush OD bias: with probability ~demand_mult-0.2, destination forced to the network center node (run.py:1741-1743). max_total_vehicles caps spawns (run.py:1726-1727).

ROUTING (roads.py): Grid = BFS by HOP COUNT (roads.py:242-257, not even metric-weighted); Custom/spider/OSM = Dijkstra by edge length with deterministic tie-break (roads.py:561-585); Ring = shorter arc (roads.py:341-344). OD models: "uniform" (rejection-sample dest ≥3 hops) or "gravity" (weight ~ exp(-(hops-min)/scale), roads.py:259-278, 620-636); optional boundary_origins spawns at perimeter nodes (roads.py:283, 641). NO congestion-aware routing, NO en-route rerouting; timed close_edge events divert only trips spawned during the closure window (run.py:1731-1736, comment at 1750-1751: "routing closures only affect the spawn pre-pass"); closures that would disconnect the graph are skipped (roads.py:201-229, 518-545). Route is FROZEN at spawn — one deterministic shortest path per OD pair, zero route diversity.

INTERSECTIONS: traffic_lights (opt-in, run.py:435-436): ALL nodes signalized or NONE. Signal = fixed 2-phase: node phase from a deterministic 2-colouring (grid checkerboard (i+j)%2, roads.py:162-170; BFS colouring for custom, roads.py:481-511), half of light_cycle_s (default 24 s) green per axis (run.py:2266-2272), axis chosen by the vehicle's instantaneous heading (abs(cos)≥abs(sin), run.py:2466). Red = virtual stopped leader 2 m before the node (run.py:2462-2470). NO yellow/all-red, NO turn phases, NO coordination/green wave, NO actuation, uniform cycle everywhere. gap_acceptance (opt-in, OFF, run.py:467-482): at UNsignalized nodes only, deterministic first-come priority (closest-to-node wins, tie by vid), conflicting = heading diff in (45°,135°) (run.py:2420-2441, 2471-2479); NOT time-gap based, no stop/yield sign distinction; with lights on it is disabled entirely (run.py:2248). turn_slowdown (opt-in, OFF, run.py:446-451): caps speed to turn_speed_mps=6 through bends ≥40° via a virtual slow leader (run.py:2480-2483; bend geometry from Trip.next_turn, roads.py:86-99). NO conflict-area physics: with lights off and gap_acceptance off, crossing streams drive through each other; turning vehicles never conflict-checked; no collision detection anywhere.

FLEET MIX: 4 classes with weights car .75 / moto .08 / truck .10 / bus .07 (run.py:142-147), custom via fleet_mix (run.py:150-168). VRUs (opt-in, vru_pct): separate wander-walk actors placed deliberately OFF-road near nodes (run.py:1642-1698), constant vru_speed 1.8 m/s, random direction — no sidewalks, no crossings, no interaction with vehicles (vehicles never brake for them; VRUs never cross roads meaningfully).

SPEEDS/HIERARCHY: default: all roads uncapped, drivers hold desired speed 8-18 m/s. Opt-in arterial_every/arterial_speed/local_speed for grid (roads.py:106-115, 172-181), whole-ring cap (roads.py:315-321), per-edge speeds in custom JSON [a,b,speed] (roads.py:405-423) and from OSM maxspeed/highway class (osm.py:39-45, 52-62). Perfect compliance, no speeding distribution.

WEATHER: WEATHER_SPEED_MULT clear 1.0/rain .85/fog .75/snow .6 applied ONLY to desired speed AT SPAWN (run.py:1587-1588); a mid-run weather event affects only NEWLY spawned drivers (acknowledged at run.py:766). No friction/braking-distance/headway effect (IDM b, T unchanged). Weather also scales GNSS noise (run.py:137) and radio loss (run.py:138).

BOUNDARY/DESPAWN: flow vehicles despawn when s_pos ≥ trip.length (finish_time set, run.py:2492-2494; removed at run.py:2535-2539 — instant vanish, no terminal decel/parking). Fixed-fleet vehicles drive straight forever off any map. Cert lifetime is budgeted from trip length + signal-wait heuristic so honest certs don't expire mid-trip (run.py:1543-1563).

NETWORKS (roads.py): GridNetwork (w×h Manhattan, optional connectivity-preserving dropout, roads.py:102-300), RingNetwork (roads.py:311-370), CustomNetwork (arbitrary undirected node/edge graph, MAX 400 nodes / 1600 edges, roads.py:383-384), spider_graph generator (roads.py:683-703), OSM importer (osm.py) that converts small real-city extracts (11 preset ~1-2 km² bboxes, osm.py:25-37) to custom networks: drivable ways → edges with speed limits, RDP-simplified at 10 m tolerance, minor road classes dropped to fit ≤380 nodes (osm.py:85-120). All edges are UNDIRECTED CENTERLINES: no one-way streets, no per-edge lane counts, opposing traffic shares the same geometry (only the ≥45° heading filter at run.py:2458 keeps them from IDM-interacting — they physically overlap/pass through each other).

V2X coupling (for context): one CAM per vehicle per step (dt=1 s default ⇒ 1 Hz beacons); reception = hard disc radio_range_m=500 or opt-in log-distance path loss + log-normal shadowing (run.py:2693-2745); losses compose: packet_loss_base + nlos_loss*d/rr + congestion (linear over chan_capacity, cap 0.8, run.py:2746-2750) + weather.

STEP LOOP STRUCTURE (run.py:2524-2965): per step — spawn/despawn (2533-2539) → car_follow (2541-2542) → broadcast pre-pass incl. GNSS measurement + attack falsification (2544-2650) → reception/detection (2673-2893) → collusion (2895-2939) → online MA revocation (2941-2955) → live viz/streaming (2957-2965).
gaps: No directional roadway model: every edge is an undirected centerline; opposing streams occupy identical geometry and simply ignore each other (heading filter run.py:2458). No one-way streets, no per-direction lanes, no median separation, no head-on interaction. This is the single largest structural gap vs a real city.

Default mode has no traffic physics at all: fixed-fleet vehicles fly straight lines with sinusoidal wander and no interaction (run.py:656-668); everything realistic (IDM, networks, signals) requires opt-in flow mode, and even there car_following can be off (Trip.state = constant speed, roads.py:74-77, vehicles overlap).

Routing is static single-shortest-path: grid uses hop-count BFS (roads.py:242-257, not even metric), custom uses length Dijkstra; no congestion-aware assignment, no stochastic route choice, no en-route rerouting or dynamic user equilibrium; road closures only divert trips spawned after the closure (run.py:1750-1751) — vehicles already en route drive through 'closed' roads.

Signal control is toy: all-or-nothing signalization, one global 2-phase fixed-time plan (half cycle per axis, default 24 s cycle), checkerboard offsets only; no yellow/all-red clearance, no protected left turns, no coordination/green waves, no actuated or adaptive control, no per-intersection plans (run.py:2266-2272, 2462-2470; roads.py:162-170, 500-511).

No intersection conflict physics: crossing/turning vehicles never collide or block each other inside the junction box; gap_acceptance (off by default) is a deterministic closest-first rule, not time-gap acceptance; no stop/yield signs, no roundabout yield-at-entry semantics, no queue spillback blocking the box (run.py:2420-2441).

Lane realism: uniform global n_lanes on every road (run.py:420); lane changes are discretionary-only MOBIL and OFF by default (run.py:453-466); no mandatory lane changes for turns, no merge/weaving at lane drops or on-ramps, no overtaking on 2-lane bidirectional roads.
No pedestrian-vehicle interaction: VRUs are off-road random-walk beacons (run.py:1642-1698); no sidewalks, crosswalks, signal-phased crossings, jaywalking, or vehicles yielding/braking for VRUs.

Demand is synthetic: homogeneous Poisson thinned by a profile mapped to run-fraction (rush peaks at 25%/75% of the RUN, not clock time, run.py:1705-1711); OD is uniform or 1-parameter hop-gravity (roads.py:259-278); no land-use/zonal OD matrices, no trip chaining, no freight/delivery/transit patterns, no weekday/weekend structure.

Driver heterogeneity is minimal: desired speed U(8,18) plus 4 class multipliers; IDM a/b/T/s0 identical within a class; no per-driver aggressiveness/headway/reaction-time distributions, no acceleration noise (SUMO sigma), no speeding or limit-compliance variance, no distracted/erratic benign drivers.

Weather barely affects driving: only spawn-time desired speed (run.py:1587-1588); mid-run weather changes do not slow existing drivers (run.py:766); no reduced friction (IDM b unchanged), no longer headways, no incident-rate coupling.

No parked/stopping traffic: no on-street parking, parking search, bus stops or transit dwell, taxi pickups, delivery double-parking; no incidents/breakdowns/accidents blocking lanes (stationary vehicles exist only as a DENM event concept).

Network scale and geometry: hard cap 400 nodes/1600 edges (roads.py:383-384); OSM import limited to ~1-2 km2 extracts simplified to <=380 nodes at 10 m tolerance with minor roads dropped first (osm.py:85-120); no curvature-continuous geometry, no elevation/grades, no roundabout topology primitives, no turn restrictions, no signalized vs unsignalized mix within one map.

Beaconing is 1 Hz at default dt=1.0 s (run.py:276), vs ETSI CAM 1-10 Hz dynamics-triggered generation rules; no DCC (decentralized congestion control) adapting beacon rate; sub-second kinematic transients (hard braking profiles) are invisible.
Despawn is teleportation at the destination node (run.py:2492-2494, 2535-2539): no terminal deceleration, parking, or destination-side congestion; fixed-fleet vehicles leave the mapped area entirely.
No collision detection or safety surrogates anywhere (no TTC/PET measures); physically overlapping vehicles are legal states.

Traffic-signal micro-behavior missing: no start-up lost time, driver reaction delay at green, or dilemma-zone behavior; axis classification from instantaneous heading (run.py:2466) misassigns diagonal edges on custom/OSM maps.
Speed behavior: perfect compliance with posted caps; speed hierarchy off by default (all roads uncapped, run.py:437-445); trip speed distribution independent of road class or context.

Radio/network realism (secondary to traffic here): NLOS is a scalar distance ratio, not building-geometry-aware; congestion loss is a per-receiver linear function (run.py:2746-2750) with no MAC/CSMA-CA, hidden-terminal, or per-packet capture modeling; no correlated shadowing (per-link i.i.d. redraw each step, run.py:2740-2744).
opportunities: SUMO/TraCI swap is feasible through a narrow seam: true kinematics are consumed ONLY via Vehicle.true_state(t) (run.py:650-668) and the cf fields cur_x/cur_y/cur_v/cur_h; car_follow() is invoked at exactly one call site (run.py:2541-2542). An adapter can set v.cf=True and write cur_x/cur_y/cur_v/cur_h from TraCI each step, set finish_time on SUMO arrival, and delete car_follow — the broadcast/detection/MA pipeline downstream is untouched.

Blockers to design around for the swap: (a) the whole sim is one ~1600-line run_pipeline closure (run.py:1413-3045) with mobility, radio, and MA logic sharing state — extract a MobilityProvider interface (spawn schedule, per-step states, despawns) first; (b) the flow spawn schedule + attacker/faulty/OD assignment is fully precomputed BEFORE the loop (run.py:1700-1751) — must become event-driven when SUMO owns insertion; (c) cert-lifetime budgeting reads trip.length (run.py:1543-1559) — replace with SUMO route length or a generous horizon; (d) the mapOffRoad detector needs net.dist_to_road (run.py:2262-2264, roads.py:183-191, 587-618) — back it with the SUMO net (sumolib lane distance); (e) byte-identical digest reproducibility (the project's core contract) is tied to Python RNG draw order — an external engine forks the determinism story, so gate it as a new mode rather than perturbing defaults; (f) PER_STEP_HOOK (run.py:1400-1402) already exists as a per-step seam but is telemetry-only.

The repo already treats SUMO-grade realism as the MOSAIC layer's job (scms-sim/, toolchain at C:/Users/Administrator/tools: SUMO 1.25.0, MOSAIC 25.2); the highest-leverage path is wiring the mock pipeline's SCMS/attack/detection passes onto TraCI states rather than re-implementing microsimulation in Python.

Pure-Python upgrades with high realism-per-effort, in the existing opt-in byte-identical pattern: (1) directed edges + per-edge lane counts in CustomNetwork (accept [a,b,speed,lanes,oneway]) so opposing traffic gets separated geometry; (2) congestion-aware routing: reroute at spawn using live per-edge mean speeds (the sim already has all positions; add an edge-occupancy accumulator), plus en-route rerouting at nodes; (3) signal plans per node: yellow+all-red intervals, per-node cycle/split/offset, actuated extension from queue presence (queue length is derivable from the cf snapshot); (4) mandatory lane changes: force lane_idx toward turn lanes within X m of a node, reusing the existing MOBIL transition machinery (run.py:2379-2399); (5) driver heterogeneity: per-vehicle draws of T, a, b, s0 and a speedFactor distribution (SUMO-style N(1,0.1)) in make_vehicle (run.py:1584-1599); (6) weather-coupled IDM (scale b and T by weather) and apply weather speed mult continuously, not at spawn; (7) VRU crossing behavior: route VRUs along edges with periodic road crossings that insert a virtual stopped leader for approaching vehicles; (8) incident events: a new events type parking a vehicle mid-lane for a window (the virtual-leader mechanism at run.py:2468-2470 is directly reusable); (9) sub-second dt + ETSI CAM triggering rules (emit CAM on delta-position/speed/heading thresholds) — the pre-pass at run.py:2544-2650 is the single place beacon cadence is decided.

OSM path is the fastest route to 'real city' topology today (osm.py CLI -> custom network with real speed limits), but raise MAX_NODES/MAX_EDGES (roads.py:383-384) and add oneway tag handling in osm_to_network (currently discarded) to make it faithful.

Radio realism hooks: reception is one well-isolated block (run.py:2673-2751) — building-aware NLOS could reuse net geometry (count edge crossings between tx/rx), correlated shadowing needs only a per-link (not per-step) RNG key at run.py:2740-2744, and a CBR-based DCC beacon-rate adaptation would slot into the pre-pass.
notes: Read all 3437 lines of run.py plus roads.py (704 lines) in full and osm.py header/converter. Design philosophy that constrains changes: every realism feature is opt-in and gated so the DEFAULT config's data_digest stays byte-identical (string-keyed dedicated RNG streams per feature, e.g. run.py:1801-1805, 2740-2744); any change to default-path RNG draw order breaks the golden digest contract, so new realism must follow the same opt-in pattern or live in a new engine mode. Presets in CLI_PRESETS (run.py:878-897) show intended 'realistic' operating points (urban_rush: 6x6 grid, 2 lanes, lights, gravity OD, 3 veh/s). The step loop's phase ordering (spawn -> mobility -> broadcast -> receive -> decide) maps 1:1 onto a TraCI simulationStep-driven loop, which is the strongest argument that an external-engine swap is architecturally cheap despite the monolithic closure. GUI/live map consumes live_state.json + network.json (run.py:2209-2235). Vehicle motion state is fully described by (cur_x, cur_y, cur_v, cur_h, s_pos, lane_off) — no acceleration state is carried between steps except implicitly via cur_v.
